kept.excerpt: Russian forces continue to infiltrate in small groups rather than conduct mechanized assaults in the Kostyantynivka-Druzhkivka tactical area. Geolocated footage published on July 16 shows Ukrainian forces striking a Russian position northwestern of Vasyutynke (northeast of Druzhkivka) after what ISW assesses was an infiltration mission. A spokesperson of a Ukrainian brigade operating in the Kostyantynivka direction reported on July 16 that Russian forces continue deploying small groups of dismounted infantry in the Kostyantynivka direction and are not conducting mechanized assaults.
kept.publisher: Institute for the Study of War / AEI Critical Threats Project
kept.relevance: The cutoff-day assessment documents infiltration tactics in the relevant tactical area, which matter because the resolution rules include ISW's assessed infiltration shading.

kept.excerpt: Russian forces continued offensive operations in the Kostyantynivka-Druzhkivka tactical area on July 14 and 15 but did not advance. Russian forces are continuing infiltration missions and strikes in Kostyantynivka but have not seized the city. A Ukrainian officer operating in the Kostyantynivka direction reported on July 15 that Russian forces do not fully control the city despite Russian officials claims that Russian forces seized Kostyantynivka.
kept.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
kept.relevance: This assessment establishes the immediate pre-cutoff situation in the neighboring city and distinguishes Russian claims from ISW's assessment of territorial progress.

kept.excerpt: Russian forces recently advanced in the Kostyantynivka-Druzhkivka tactical area, as Ukrainian forces counterattacked in the area. Geolocated footage published on July 13 indicates that Russian forces recently advanced in western Kostyantynivka.
kept.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
kept.relevance: Geolocated Russian gains and Ukrainian counterattacks provide evidence of the local advance trajectory toward the area south of Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka.

kept.excerpt: Russian forces are intensifying their strikes against Druzhkivka to prepare the battlefield and force civilians to evacuate. Donetsk Oblast Military Administration Head Vadym Filashkin stated on July 13 that Russian forces are increasing the number of guided glide bomb, artillery, Shahed drone, Gerbera drone, and fiber optic drone strikes against Donetsk Oblast and that the situation in the region is most difficult in Druzhkivka. Filashkin noted that Russian forces are trying to take control of the access roads leading to Druzhkivka and Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka (between Druzhkivka and Kostyantynivka).
kept.publisher: Institute for the Study of War / AEI Critical Threats Project
kept.relevance: The regional administration's report directly identifies pressure on Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka's access roads, a relevant precursor to a ground entry.

kept.excerpt: It is highly unlikely that Russia has fully secured Kostiantynivka. Instead, it is assessed that Russia likely occupies approximately over half of the urban centre. Open source reporting has identified incidents of Russian flag raising along the northern boundary of the city, but these are highly likely small infiltration groups rather than a consolidated force. It is highly likely that Ukraine continues to defend the city, disrupting Russia’s ability to seize full control.
kept.publisher: Kyiv Post, reproducing British Defence Intelligence's July 10, 2026 update
kept.relevance: British Defence Intelligence offers an additional assessment of Russian proximity and the distinction between infiltrators and consolidated forces in the neighboring urban battlefield.

kept.excerpt: Russia’s spring-summer 2026 offensive has failed to achieve operationally significant gains thus far, and Russian forces’ rate of advance in June 2026 is a fraction of the rate of advance that Russian forces achieved in June 2025. ISW has observed evidence to assess that Russian forces seized or infiltrated 30.42 square kilometers in June 2026 and advanced or infiltrated at an average pace of 1.01 square kilometers per day. Russian forces comparatively seized 481.25 square kilometers in June 2025, advancing at an average pace of 16.04 square kilometers per day. Russian forces’ main territorial gains have been in Russia’s main effort area near Kostyantynivka in Donetsk Oblast, where Russian forces have achieved slow tactical gains at high costs in the city’s urban environs.
kept.publisher: Institute for the Study of War / AEI Critical Threats Project
kept.relevance: The contemporaneous advance-rate comparison supplies a historical baseline while identifying Kostyantynivka as the concentration of Russian gains.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-16, inclusive. Selected six dated publications; excluded later-dated and undated sources, prediction-market pages, odds, and market prices. Excerpts retain source attribution and uncertainty. The Kyiv Post item was published July 14 and reproduces an intelligence update dated July 10. Publication dates and passages were verified through web_search results containing dated source text. Direct web_fetch failed because of provider configuration; the agent-reach skill web-reading fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so no successful full-page fetch is claimed. The live ISW map was not used as a historical snapshot, and qualifying settlement shading or persistence through a subsequent daily update was not independently verified. These items provide contemporaneous forecasting evidence, not a resolution determination.
